task_completion_reasoning: The assistant clearly completed all user goals: confirming card charges, locking the lost card, ordering a replacement with chosen shipping, providing watch order status, and blocking the stolen SIM with device details.

criteria.criterion: The agent handles the second interruption (SIM block request) without losing track of the still-open Galaxy Watch order question
criteria.reasoning: After answering the Galaxy Watch question, the agent handles the SIM interruption and later explicitly resumes the prior River Visa replacement flow ("Would you like to continue with the replacement for your lost River Visa ending 4821?"), showing it did not lose track of the pre-interruption task state while the watch status question remained answered and not dropped.

criteria.criterion: The agent respects the customer's decision not to order a SIM replacement yet, without insisting or placing one anyway. ORD-20260701-004 is an existing open replacement nano-SIM already on the account. Seeing it in the order list is not a new order. The agent fails only if it places a new replacement or tells the customer a new SIM was ordered after they declined.
criteria.reasoning: When the user says "I’m okay without a replacement SIM for now, thanks.", the bot replies "No problem — your SIM will remain blocked, and you can request a replacement anytime." and the ledger shows only `finish_task()` for sim_management with no replacement-SIM tool calls, so no new SIM is ordered or pushed.

criteria.criterion: After the SIM digression, the agent returns to and answers the original Galaxy Watch order status question rather than dropping it
criteria.reasoning: The Galaxy Watch status question was already fully answered before the SIM digression; after the SIM flow ends the agent returns to the card replacement flow ("Would you like to continue with the replacement for your lost River Visa ending 4821"), not to the already-answered watch question, so there is no post-SIM return or restatement of the watch status to evaluate and the requirement as phrased is not met.

criteria.criterion: The agent does not re-ask which card to replace or why it needs replacing after the customer has already named the River Visa and said it is lost. Continuing or re-asking the open fraud-review step (whether recent charges look familiar) after digression is expected — the customer interrupted before answering. Fail if the agent restarts card selection or reason collection, or re-asks steps already completed in this conversation (for example fraud verdict, lock consent, shipping), as if starting a new replacement.
criteria.reasoning: Post-digression the agent resumes with the fraud-review question only ("These were the most recent charges... Do all of these look familiar"), without re-asking which card, why it needs replacing, or any previously completed steps like reason, lock consent, or shipping.

criteria.criterion: The card replacement order is confirmed by the end of the conversation, and the agent audibly shares its order ID. Accept letters spoken as words, digit-by-digit readings, grouping differences, and minor ASR/phonetic transcription mismatches; fail only if the ID is omitted or not recognizably consistent with the returned value.
criteria.reasoning: After recording standard shipping and running `process_card_replacement`, the bot tells the user "Your replacement River Visa ending 4821 has been ordered with standard shipping. Your order ID is RPL-2026-001843" and reiterates it in a summary, matching the ledger’s `replacement_order_summary` Order ID.
